# Rotate Image

- Route: `/tools/rotate-image`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `rotate-image`

## Summary

Turn a photo 90°, 180° or 270°, fix a sideways scan or phone picture, and download it in any format. (Image tools)

## Details

Phones record orientation as a tag that some viewers ignore, and scanners and old cameras get it wrong outright. Rotating the pixels themselves fixes it for good. Media Manipulator rotates images on our servers with ImageMagick by 90, 180, 270 or 45 degrees, honours the existing orientation tag first, and exports in any format.
### What it does
- Rotates by 90° (clockwise), 180°, 270° (counter-clockwise) or 45°.
- Bakes the rotation into the pixels and clears the EXIF orientation tag.
- Combine with crop, resize and format conversion.
- Write the turned image as JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or GIF.
### How to use it
1. Upload an image: Any common format.
2. Pick the angle: 90° is preselected.
3. Convert: ImageMagick rotates and encodes.
4. Download: Save the upright image.
### Supported formats
- Input: jpg, png, webp, gif, avif, heic, bmp, tiff
- Output: jpg, png, webp, avif, gif
### Technical details
- The existing EXIF orientation is applied first, so what you see is what gets rotated.
- A 45° rotation adds a background fill at the corners; crop afterwards if needed.
- Use the Flip & mirror tools for horizontal or vertical mirroring instead.
### Use cases
- Sideways phone photo: Rotate 90° so it is upright everywhere.
- Upside-down scan: Rotate 180°.
- Fix a form upload: Rotate before submitting a document photo.
- Tilted effect: Rotate 45° for a design element.
### FAQ
Q: Why does my photo look upright on my phone but sideways elsewhere?
A: Your phone wrote an orientation tag that the other app ignores. Rotating here bakes the orientation into the pixels.
Q: Does rotating lose quality?
A: Rotation by 90° multiples is lossless in geometry; the re-encode is the only cost. Use PNG or high JPG quality.
Q: Can I rotate by an arbitrary angle?
A: Only 45° plus the 90° multiples are offered.
Q: Can I mirror instead?
A: Not here; mirroring is not currently offered for images.
